newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher on Greenspan comments.

* Toronto stocks soared on Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan eased investor fears of a rate hike that might slow Wall Street's advance * 114 million shares traded.
Toronto stocks soared along with U.S. equities on Wednesday amid waning fears of a U.S. interest rate hike that might slow Wall Street's advance.
The TSE 300 Index jumped 48.07 points to close at 6203.12 in brisk turnover of 114.2 million shares worth C$2.1 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed its Canadian neighbor, soaring over 93 points to finish around 6945.

"Basically, he (Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan) was saying that the market is not overvalued," said Ira Katzin with RBC Dominion Securities. Greenspan said the market was "properly priced" if Wall Street's profit estimates were right.
"We don't view monetary policy as a tool to...prick the stock market bubble, or something like that," Greenspan told the U.S. House of Representatives Banking Subcommittee on Wednesday.

In an address to the National Association of Business Economists earlier, Greenspan denied he was trying to talk down stock markets when he suggested both last week and in December that stock prices may be too lofty.
In today's action, Toronto posted gains in 12 of 14 sub-groups including banks, communications, conglomerates and consumer products. The weak groups were gold and forestry.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Royal Bank of Canada jumped 2.05 to 57.70 on 1.1 million shares after Canada's largest bank reported sharply higher first quarter profits. A proposal to limit executive pay at the bank was defeated at Royal Bank's annual meeting in Vancouver earlier today.
* Among other bank stocks, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce rose 1.20 to 67.10. Bank of Montreal climbed 1.15 to close at 50.60 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 50.80.
* Remington Energy rose 2 to 22.10 after its C$200 million acquisition of B.C. Star Partners' assets in British Columbia.
